text:
sasha: Noticed an ~8-12% latency regression on short seqs (<128) after enabling FlashAttention v3 in the canary. Can we triage? cc @maria @kevin
maria: Yup, saw it in the dashboard. seq=64 throughput drops, p95 up. Quick numbers: baseline (v2) p95=60ms, v3 p95=68ms. GPU util roughly same.
kevin: Hmm. Would expect v3 to be better. Can you paste the nsys/nvprof traces and any kernel call logs?
sasha: Attached short-run profile (nsys). Main anomaly: stalls around kernel `fmha_v3` and an extra memcpy pattern between kernels.
ryan: That smells like workspace alloc churn. v3 expanded workspace allocation pattern for some optimizations; many small batches can trigger repeated malloc/free + kernel launch overhead. Is the workspace pool enabled on the canary?
maria: We intentionally disabled workspace pool for the canary to avoid cross-tenant reuse — might be the culprit.
sasha: I re-ran with workspace pool enabled on the same machines: p95 improved to ~62ms. So pool reduces the regression but question remains why v2 didn't hit this.
kevin: v2 uses a smaller ephemeral buffer and fuses the alloc path more aggressively. v3 introduced a per-call workspace tracker for causal-mask/fused-softmax optimizations which increases allocation count if pool isn't present.
ryan: Suggestion: update kernel-selection heuristics. If seq_len < 128 AND workspace_pool == disabled -> prefer flashattn-v2. Alternatively, make pool `enabled` default when v3 is selected.
maria: Also note v3 picks a different kernel variant when model_dim=1024 that increases shared memory usage; it's fine on A100 80GB but will be heavier on older cards (T4/RTX). We should surface that in compatibility docs.
sasha: Action items:
- change fallback rule: short-seq + pool disabled -> fallback to flashattn-v2 (owner: kevin)
- docs + deploy note: workspace pool recommendation when using v3 (owner: maria)
- add kernel telemetry (owner: ryan) to capture choice + seq bucket + pool state
kevin: I'll open a PR for heuristics. Quick question: what's the canonical config flag path? `runtime.workers.workspace_pool.enabled`?
maria: We currently use `runtime.memory.workspace_pool` with values `enabled|disabled|auto`. Let's use `auto` default; when `auto` and v3 selected, enable the pool.
ryan: I'll add a compact telemetry event `kernel.choice` with fields: `kernel=v3|v2`, `seq_bucket=<32|64|128|256+>`, `pool_state=enabled|disabled|auto`. Keep payload <200 bytes.
sasha: Canary plan: roll 10% traffic with v3+pool enabled, and concurrently 10% with v3+pool disabled to validate the fallback rule behavior. deploy-bot: can you create two canaries?
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued. Created canaries: canary-a (v3+pool) id:c-18421a, canary-b (v3+no-pool) id:c-18421b. Perf hooks wired to perf-bot.
perf-bot: Perf dashboards created: short-seq (seq64), seq128, long-seq. Alerts: fire if p95 regresses >5% vs baseline for 30m. Posting hourly summaries to #eng-runtime.
maria: One more note: quantized kernels (int8/fp8 paths) on v3 showed ~3% token throughput regression in our pre-release quant tests. Might be separate tuning knob (scale/writeback).
kevin: Good catch — I'll gate quantized model rollouts behind the same heuristic for now.
sasha: Thanks — big wins if we keep v3 for long seqs and v2 for tiny seqs when pool disabled. Sync tomorrow 10:00 to review canary results. :thumbsup:
